Size type used by the library; either size_t or 32-bit unsigned depending on configuration.
Boolean integer type (0/1). True/False macros provided.
Single-byte input interface. Implementations provide a Read function returning a byte; 0 indicates EOF/error.
Single-byte output interface. Implementations provide Write to emit one byte.
Sequential input stream interface. Read fills a buffer up to size; helper functions provided to read exact sizes/bytes.
Sequential output stream interface with Write that returns number of bytes written.
Seek origin enumeration used by seek-capable stream interfaces.
Seekable input stream interface combining sequential Read and Seek operations.
Buffered look-ahead input stream interface providing Look/Skip, direct Read, and Seek. Helper functions assist with typical read/seek operations.

Adapter that wraps an ISeekInStream to provide an ILookInStream interface with internal buffer. Caller must supply buf and bufSize; initialize pos and size with LookToRead2_Init and set function table via LookToRead2_CreateVTable.
Adapter that exposes an ILookInStream as an ISeqInStream (look-to-seq). VTable is set with SecToLook_CreateVTable.
Adapter that exposes an ILookInStream as an ISeqInStream for direct reading. VTable is set with SecToRead_CreateVTable.
Progress callback interface for compression/decompression operations, reporting input/output sizes and allowing early termination.

objects.definition:

#ifdef _LZMA_PROB32
  UInt32
#else
  UInt16
#endif
  CLzmaProb;
objects.description: Probability type used by the LZMA range decoder. It is a 16-bit value by default, or 32-bit if _LZMA_PROB32 is defined, impacting memory usage and potentially speed.
Holds LZMA coder properties: literal context bits (lc), literal position bits (lp), position bits (pb), and dictionary size (dicSize). Used to configure/initialize the decoder.

Opaque-ish LZMA decoder state object holding properties, probability tables, dictionary buffer, range decoder state, and temporary buffers. Must be constructed, allocated, initialized, used for decoding, and freed using the provided API. The structure layout is fixed because of possible ASM usage; client code should not modify internal fields except as documented (e.g., dic/dicPos in dictionary interface).
Controls how strictly the decoder must reach stream end when the output limit is hit: either stop anywhere or require the block to finish at the limit.
Output-only status code reporting how decoding finished or whether more input is required.

objects.definition:
typedef struct _CLzmaEncProps
{
  int level;       /* 0 <= level <= 9 */
  UInt32 dictSize; /* (1 << 12) <= dictSize <= (1 << 27) for 32-bit version
                      (1 << 12) <= dictSize <= (3 << 29) for 64-bit version
                      default = (1 << 24) */
  int lc;          /* 0 <= lc <= 8, default = 3 */
  int lp;          /* 0 <= lp <= 4, default = 0 */
  int pb;          /* 0 <= pb <= 4, default = 2 */
  int algo;        /* 0 - fast, 1 - normal, default = 1 */
  int fb;          /* 5 <= fb <= 273, default = 32 */
  int btMode;      /* 0 - hashChain Mode, 1 - binTree mode - normal, default = 1 */
  int numHashBytes; /* 2, 3 or 4, default = 4 */
  UInt32 mc;       /* 1 <= mc <= (1 << 30), default = 32 */
  unsigned writeEndMark;  /* 0 - do not write EOPM, 1 - write EOPM, default = 0 */
  int numThreads;  /* 1 or 2, default = 2 */

  UInt64 reduceSize; /* estimated size of data that will be compressed. default = (UInt64)(Int64)-1.
                        Encoder uses this value to reduce dictionary size */
} CLzmaEncProps;
objects.description: Encoder property structure for configuring LZMA compression (dictionary size, literal context bits, algorithm mode, match finder options, threading, and optional end marker). Values outside documented ranges result in parameter errors when applied. Use with LzmaEnc_SetProps or one-call LzmaEncode.

objects.definition: typedef void * CLzmaEncHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an internal LZMA encoder instance. Must be created with LzmaEnc_Create and destroyed with LzmaEnc_Destroy. Used with the LzmaEnc_* API to perform encoding and query/write properties.

State object for an LZMA2 decoder instance. It stores the LZMA2 parser/control state, chunk sizes, and embeds a CLzmaDec (LZMA1) decoder used to decode LZMA chunks within the LZMA2 stream. Fields include control/status bytes, sizes of current pack/unpack chunks, and the underlying LZMA decoder state.
Enum of LZMA2 parsing statuses returned by Lzma2Dec_Parse in addition to standard LZMA status codes. Indicates boundaries: start of a new independent block or a new chunk header detected.

Properties/configuration for the LZMA2 encoder, including embedded LZMA properties, target block size, per-block threading limits, and total thread count. Used to configure an encoder instance before encoding. Detailed semantics of each field follow typical 7-Zip LZMA2 conventions; specific constraints are not documented in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void * CLzma2EncHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an LZMA2 encoder instance. It is created and destroyed via the provided API and used with encode-related functions. The underlying structure is intentionally hidden (void pointer).
Filter descriptor in an XZ block, holding the filter ID and its property bytes.
Represents an XZ block header fields and its filter chain, plus optional sizes and flags.
Incremental checksum context used by XZ (CRC32, CRC64, or SHA-256 depending on stream flags).

objects.definition: typedef UInt16 CXzStreamFlags;
objects.description: 16-bit flags field of an XZ stream; lower nibble encodes the Check type.
Holds per-block unpacked size and total (packed+overhead) size for an XZ stream index.
Represents a single XZ stream with its flags and a list of block sizes parsed from the index.
Container of multiple XZ streams, typically when concatenated streams are present.
Status codes returned by decoders; mirrors ELzmaStatus for LZMA2.
Finish policy for decoding operations; mirrors ELzmaFinishMode.
Vtable-like interface for stateful coders/filters (e.g., LZMA2, delta, x86), including lifecycle, property setting, coding, and optional in-place filter function.
Manages a chain of up to 4 filters/coders, their buffers, states, and statuses for XZ block decoding.

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
  XZ_STATE_STREAM_HEADER,
  XZ_STATE_STREAM_INDEX,
  XZ_STATE_STREAM_INDEX_CRC,
  XZ_STATE_STREAM_FOOTER,
  XZ_STATE_STREAM_PADDING,
  XZ_STATE_BLOCK_HEADER,
  XZ_STATE_BLOCK,
  XZ_STATE_BLOCK_FOOTER
} EXzState;
objects.description: State machine for the high-level XZ stream/unpacker parsing and decoding process.
High-level XZ unpacker context holding parser state, current block info, filter chain (CMixCoder), checksum contexts, and optional direct output buffer control.
Properties for multi-threaded XZ decoding, including ST/MT buffer sizes, thread count, and memory cap.

objects.definition: typedef void * CXzDecMtHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a multi-threaded XZ decoder instance created/destroyed by the MT API.
Collects statistics and result codes from a decoding session, including sizes, counts, and combined result type.

Properties for an optional XZ filter stage (e.g., Delta or BCJ). Contains filter ID and filter-specific parameters. ip/ipDefined suggest instruction-pointer–relative transforms (e.g., BCJ). Exact semantics depend on the filter id and are not fully documented in this header.

Top-level encoder properties for XZ encoding. Wraps LZMA2 encoder properties and optional filter properties, along with container-level settings such as checksum type (checkId), block size, threading configuration, header size writing policy, and optional reduction/target size.

objects.definition: typedef void * CXzEncHandle;
objects.description: Opaque handle for an XZ encoder instance managed by the API. It must be created via XzEnc_Create and destroyed with XzEnc_Destroy. It is an alias of void*, treated as an opaque pointer by users.
Simple view over a contiguous memory buffer containing 7z-encoded data. Holds pointer and size; does not own the memory.

Descriptor for a coder (compression method) used in a folder. Stores the method ID, number of streams, and where coder properties are located along with their size. Supports only default methods per comment.
Represents a connection (bond) between coder streams within a folder, mapping an output stream index to an input stream index.

Describes a 7z folder (a group of coders and streams forming a decoding pipeline). Holds coders, their bonds, pack stream indices, and the index of the main unpack stream. Array sizes are limited by the SZ_NUM_* macros in this header.
NTFS FILETIME split into low/high 32-bit parts (little-endian). Used to store file timestamps.
Bitmask-with-values helper: Defs is a bit array (MSB-first per byte) that indicates presence of values; Vals stores corresponding UInt32 values for set bits.
Bitmask-with-values helper for 64-bit fields, here storing timestamp values as CNtfsFileTime entries. Defs indicates which entries are present.

Core in-archive structure describing folders and pack streams. Contains counts and multiple arrays indexing coder data, pack positions, CRCs, and sizes. Does not own I/O; used to compute sizes and decode folders.

Extended 7z archive database with file-level metadata and indices. Embeds CSzAr and adds file counts, directory flags, CRCs, attributes, timestamps, folder-file mapping, and UTF-16LE file name storage.

functions.name: SeqInStream_Read
functions.signature: SRes SeqInStream_Read(const ISeqInStream *stream, void *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from a sequential input stream into buf. Helper over ISeqInStream::Read that requests an exact byte count via value-sized size parameter. It can return SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF to signal end-of-stream encountered during the read.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ISeqInStream instance whose Read callback is set.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes when size > 0.
size may be 0; in that case no bytes are read (behavior not explicitly documented).
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values, including SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF as a possible end-of-stream indicator.

functions.name: SeqInStream_Read2
functions.signature: SRes SeqInStream_Read2(const ISeqInStream *stream, void *buf, size_t size, SRes errorType);
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from a sequential input stream into buf using ISeqInStream::Read. On error or special conditions, returns an SRes, potentially using the provided errorType. Intended to enforce a specific error mapping while reading an exact number of bytes.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ISeqInStream instance whose Read callback is set.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes when size > 0.
Caller must provide an errorType that is a valid SRes code to be returned on read failure/EOF as defined by the implementation (exact mapping not documented here).
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values.

functions.name: SeqInStream_ReadByte
functions.description: Reads a single byte from a sequential input stream into *buf. Convenience wrapper over ISeqInStream::Read for one-byte reads. It can return SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF on end-of-stream or another SRes on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ISeqInStream instance whose Read callback is set.
buf must be a valid, writable pointer to at least 1 byte.
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values, including SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF.

functions.name: LookInStream_LookRead
functions.description: Attempts to read (peek and copy) up to *size bytes from a lookahead-capable input stream into buf using ILookInStream::Look, then advances via ILookInStream::Skip as needed. On return, *size is updated with the number of bytes actually provided/copied.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ILookInStream with Look and Skip callbacks set.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least *size bytes on entry when *size > 0.
size must be a non-NULL pointer; on input it specifies the requested number of bytes, and on output it receives the number of bytes actually read.
Caller must respect ILookInStream::Look contract: if input(*size) != 0 and output(*size) == 0, it indicates end_of_stream; output(*size) < input(*size) is allowed.
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values.

functions.name: LookInStream_SeekTo
functions.description: Seeks the lookahead-capable input stream to the absolute position offset. Utility around ILookInStream::Seek to move to a specific location.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ILookInStream with Seek callback set.
offset is a UInt64 position; behavior for values beyond stream size is implementation-defined (not documented here).
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values.

functions.name: LookInStream_Read2
functions.signature: SRes LookInStream_Read2(const ILookInStream *stream, void *buf, size_t size, SRes errorType);
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from a lookahead-capable input stream via ILookInStream::Read (direct read, not via look buffer). Returns an SRes indicating success or failure, potentially using errorType to signal a specific error on read failure/EOF.
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ILookInStream with Read callback set.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes when size > 0.
Caller must provide an errorType that is a valid SRes to be returned on read failure as defined by the implementation (exact mapping not documented here).
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values.

functions.name: LookInStream_Read
functions.signature: SRes LookInStream_Read(const ILookInStream *stream, void *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Reads up to size bytes from a lookahead-capable input stream into buf using ILookInStream::Read (direct read, bypassing the look buffer).
requirements: stream must be a valid, initialized ILookInStream with Read callback set.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes when size > 0.
Caller must handle non-SZ_OK SRes return values.

functions.name: LookToRead2_CreateVTable
functions.description: Initializes the vtable (ILookInStream interface) of a CLookToRead2 adapter that wraps an ISeekInStream as a lookahead-capable stream. The lookahead parameter controls whether the adapter provides look-ahead functionality.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a CLookToRead2 structure.
Before using the resulting stream, the following CLookToRead2 fields must be set by the caller: realStream (the underlying ISeekInStream), buf (buffer pointer), bufSize (buffer size).
Call LookToRead2_Init(p) to reset internal positions before first use or reuse.
lookahead must be a valid flag value as expected by the implementation (exact accepted values are not documented here).

functions.name: SecToLook_CreateVTable
functions.description: Initializes the vtable (ISeqInStream interface) of a CSecToLook adapter that presents an ILookInStream as a sequential input stream.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a CSecToLook structure.
Before using the resulting stream, p->realStream must be set to a valid ILookInStream instance.

functions.name: SecToRead_CreateVTable
functions.description: Initializes the vtable (ISeqInStream interface) of a CSecToRead adapter that presents an ILookInStream as a sequential input stream using direct Read operations.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a CSecToRead structure.
Before using the resulting stream, p->realStream must be set to a valid ILookInStream instance.

functions.name: LzmaCompress
functions.signature: int MY_STD_CALL LzmaCompress(unsigned char *dest, size_t *destLen, const unsigned char *src, size_t srcLen, unsigned char *outProps, size_t *outPropsSize, int level, unsigned dictSize, int lc, int lp, int pb, int fb, int numThreads);
functions.description: Compresses the input buffer using the LZMA algorithm and writes the compressed bytes to dest. On success, updates *destLen with the number of bytes written and writes the 5‑byte encoder properties into outProps (and sets *outPropsSize accordingly). Typical usage: allocate an output buffer large enough for worst-case compressed size, set *outPropsSize to 5, choose parameters (or pass -1 or 0 where allowed to use defaults), and call the function. Returns SZ_OK on success or an SZ_ERROR_* code on failure. Notes: LZMA properties are always 5 bytes. Default values are used for parameters set to -1 (level, lc, lp, pb, fb, numThreads) or 0 (dictSize). Fast mode (algo = 0) can use only 1 thread; normal mode can use up to 2 threads.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the compressed data; otherwise the function returns SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF.
destLen must be a valid pointer; on input it must contain the capacity (in bytes) of dest; on output it is set to the number of bytes actually written.
src must point to the input data buffer of size srcLen bytes; srcLen must be the exact size of the data to compress.
outProps must point to a writable buffer with capacity at least LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5) bytes.
outPropsSize must be a valid pointer; on input, *outPropsSize must be exactly LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5); on output it is set to LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5).
level must be in the range 0 <= level <= 9, or -1 to request the default (5).
dictSize may be 0 to request the default (1 << 24); otherwise it must fit platform limits (max 128 MB on 32-bit, max 1 GB on 64-bit).
lc must be in the range 0 <= lc <= 8, or -1 for default (3).
lp must be in the range 0 <= lp <= 4, or -1 for default (0).
pb must be in the range 0 <= pb <= 4, or -1 for default (2).
fb must be in the range 5 <= fb <= 273, or -1 for default (32).
numThreads must be 1 or 2, or -1 for default (2).
If the encoder selects fast mode (algo = 0), numThreads must be 1; otherwise the call may fail (only fast mode restriction stated).

Caller must check the return value: SZ_OK indicates success; SZ_ERROR_MEM indicates memory allocation failure; SZ_ERROR_PARAM indicates invalid parameter(s); SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF indicates the output buffer was too small; SZ_ERROR_THREAD indicates multithreading errors (only for multithreaded version).

functions.name: LzmaUncompress
functions.signature: int MY_STD_CALL LzmaUncompress(unsigned char *dest, size_t *destLen, const unsigned char *src, SizeT *srcLen, const unsigned char *props, size_t propsSize);
functions.description: Decompresses LZMA-compressed data from src into dest using the provided LZMA properties. On success, updates *destLen with the number of bytes written and *srcLen with the number of input bytes consumed. Typical usage: set *destLen to the capacity of dest, set *srcLen to the available input size, pass the 5‑byte properties buffer from compression (props, propsSize = 5), and call the function. Returns SZ_OK on success or an SZ_ERROR_* code on failure.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer; on input *destLen must be set to its capacity in bytes; on output *destLen is set to the number of bytes written.
src must point to the input buffer; on input *srcLen must be set to the number of available input bytes; on output *srcLen is set to the number of bytes actually consumed.
props must point to the LZMA properties buffer produced by the encoder; propsSize must be exactly 5 bytes (LZMA_PROPS_SIZE).

Caller must check the return value: SZ_OK indicates success; SZ_ERROR_DATA indicates data error; SZ_ERROR_MEM indicates memory allocation error; SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED indicates unsupported properties; SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF indicates more input bytes are needed.
Buffers must not overlap in an undefined manner; dest must not alias src in a way that corrupts decoding (standard decompressor expectation).
The provided dest capacity must be sufficient for the decompressed output; otherwise the call will fail (size handling via return codes).

functions.name: LzmaProps_Decode
functions.signature: SRes LzmaProps_Decode(CLzmaProps *p, const Byte *data, unsigned size);
functions.description: Decodes LZMA properties from a byte buffer into a CLzmaProps structure. Use this on the 5-byte properties block (LZMA_PROPS_SIZE) typically found in LZMA headers. Returns SZ_OK on success or SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for invalid/unsupported properties.
requirements: p must point to a writable CLzmaProps structure.
data must point to a buffer containing LZMA properties bytes.
size should be the exact number of property bytes provided; typical value is LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5).
Caller must handle return codes: SZ_OK or SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED.
Do not pass NULL pointers for p or data.

functions.name: LzmaDec_Init
functions.description: Initializes the LZMA decoder state for a new stream using an already-allocated CLzmaDec. Call this before starting to decode a new stream, after allocation. In the Dictionary Interface, you will then drive decoding via LzmaDec_DecodeToDic and manually manage dicPos.
requirements: p must refer to a CLzmaDec that was constructed (LzmaDec_Construct) and allocated (via LzmaDec_Allocate or LzmaDec_AllocateProbs with a valid dictionary) before calling.
Call once per new stream before any decode calls.
Do not mix interface groups for the same object (Dictionary vs Buffer).

functions.name: LzmaDec_AllocateProbs
functions.signature: SRes LzmaDec_AllocateProbs(CLzmaDec *p, const Byte *props, unsigned propsSize, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes the probability model and decoder state from LZMA properties, without allocating the dictionary buffer. Use this when you will provide and manage the dictionary buffer yourself (Dictionary Interface variant 2).
requirements: p must be constructed (LzmaDec_Construct) prior to allocation.
props must point to the LZMA properties block; propsSize should correspond to the size of that block (typically LZMA_PROPS_SIZE = 5).
alloc must be a valid allocator matching the corresponding FreeProbs call.
On success, caller must set up the dictionary buffer (p->dic, dicBufSize) manually before decoding.
Handle return codes: SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED.
Do not mix interface groups for the same object (Dictionary vs Buffer).

functions.name: LzmaDec_FreeProbs
functions.description: Frees resources allocated by LzmaDec_AllocateProbs (probability model and related state). Does not free any user-managed dictionary buffer.
requirements: p must be the same decoder object previously passed to LzmaDec_AllocateProbs.
alloc must match the allocator used in LzmaDec_AllocateProbs.
Safe to call when cleaning up after using the Dictionary Interface variant 2.

functions.name: LzmaDec_Allocate
functions.signature: SRes LzmaDec_Allocate(CLzmaDec *p, const Byte *props, unsigned propsSize, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: Allocates the full LZMA decoder state, including probability model and internal dictionary buffer, from the provided properties. Required when using the Buffer Interface; also usable for the Dictionary Interface variant 1.
requirements: p must be constructed (LzmaDec_Construct) before allocation.
props must point to the LZMA properties block; propsSize should correspond to that block (typically LZMA_PROPS_SIZE = 5).
alloc must be a valid allocator matching the corresponding Free call.
For Buffer Interface usage, this allocation variant is mandatory.
Handle return codes: SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED.
Do not mix interface groups for the same object (Dictionary vs Buffer).

functions.name: LzmaDec_Free
functions.description: Frees all resources allocated by LzmaDec_Allocate for the decoder, including the internal dictionary and probability model.
requirements: p must be the same decoder object previously passed to LzmaDec_Allocate.
alloc must match the allocator used in LzmaDec_Allocate.
Call once you are done with the decoder to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: LzmaDec_DecodeToDic
functions.signature: SRes LzmaDec_DecodeToDic(CLzmaDec *p, SizeT dicLimit, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status);
functions.description: Decodes LZMA-compressed input into the decoder’s internal dictionary buffer up to dicLimit bytes. This is the low-level Dictionary Interface; the caller consumes data directly from p->dic and must manage p->dicPos updates when dicPos reaches dicBufSize. Reports stream finishing and input needs via status.
requirements: p must be allocated and initialized (LzmaDec_Allocate[...] then LzmaDec_Init). For AllocateProbs usage, the dictionary buffer (p->dic and dicBufSize) must be set up by the caller before decoding.

dicLimit specifies the output limit in the dictionary; finishMode applies only when decoding reaches dicLimit: LZMA_FINISH_ANY decodes up to dicLimit; LZMA_FINISH_END requires the stream to finish exactly at dicLimit.
src must point to input bytes; *srcLen is an in/out parameter indicating available input on entry and bytes consumed on return.
status must point to an ELzmaStatus to receive decode status (e.g., FINISHED_WITH_MARK, NOT_FINISHED, NEEDS_MORE_INPUT, MAYBE_FINISHED_WITHOUT_MARK).
Return codes: SZ_OK on success (with status set as above) or SZ_ERROR_DATA for data errors.
Caller must manually update p->dicPos after reading from dictionary and if it reaches p->dicBufSize.
Do not mix interface groups for the same object (Dictionary vs Buffer).

functions.name: LzmaDec_DecodeToBuf
functions.signature: SRes LzmaDec_DecodeToBuf(CLzmaDec *p, Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status);
functions.description: Decodes LZMA-compressed input into a caller-provided output buffer, similar to zlib-style streaming. Use this Buffer Interface with a decoder allocated via LzmaDec_Allocate. Reports stream finishing and input needs via status.
requirements: p must be allocated via LzmaDec_Allocate and initialized with LzmaDec_Init before decoding.
dest must point to a writable buffer; *destLen is an in/out parameter indicating available output space on entry and bytes produced on return.
src must point to input bytes; *srcLen is an in/out parameter indicating available input on entry and bytes consumed on return.
finishMode applies only when decoding reaches the output limit (*destLen): LZMA_FINISH_ANY decodes up to *destLen; LZMA_FINISH_END requires the stream to finish exactly at *destLen.
status must point to an ELzmaStatus to receive the decode status.
Return code semantics match those described for the dictionary/buffer interfaces (SZ_OK or SZ_ERROR_DATA).
Do not mix interface groups for the same object (Dictionary vs Buffer).

functions.name: LzmaDecode
functions.signature: SRes LzmaDecode(Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, const Byte *propData, unsigned propSize, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: One-call LZMA decoder that allocates internally and decodes from src to dest using the provided LZMA properties. Suitable when you have complete buffers and want a single-shot decode. Reports finish status and handles allocation internally.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer; *destLen is an in/out parameter indicating available output space on entry and bytes written on return.
src must point to input bytes; *srcLen is an in/out parameter indicating available input on entry and bytes consumed on return.
propData must point to the LZMA properties block; propSize should match its length (typically LZMA_PROPS_SIZE = 5).
finishMode applies only when decoding reaches the output limit (*destLen). Use LZMA_FINISH_END if the output buffer is expected to end at the block boundary; otherwise use LZMA_FINISH_ANY.
status must point to an ELzmaStatus to receive decode status (FINISHED_WITH_MARK, NOT_FINISHED, MAYBE_FINISHED_WITHOUT_MARK).
alloc must be a valid allocator for any internal allocations.
Handle return codes: SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_DATA, SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED, SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF.

functions.name: LzmaEncProps_Init
functions.description: Initializes an LZMA encoder properties structure to documented defaults (e.g., dictSize = 1<<24, lc=3, lp=0, pb=2, algo=1, fb=32, btMode=1, numHashBytes=4, mc=32, writeEndMark=0, numThreads=2, reduceSize = (UInt64)(Int64)-1). Use this before modifying fields or passing to the encoder.
requirements: p must be a non-null pointer to a writable CLzmaEncProps struct.
Call before LzmaEnc_SetProps to ensure valid defaults.

functions.name: LzmaEncProps_Normalize
functions.description: Normalizes fields in CLzmaEncProps, clamping or adjusting them to valid ranges and defaults as documented for each field. Use after editing properties manually to ensure they meet encoder expectations.
requirements: p must be a non-null pointer to a writable CLzmaEncProps struct.

Fields will be adjusted to fit documented ranges: level [0..9], dictSize within platform limits, lc [0..8], lp [0..4], pb [0..4], algo ∈ {0,1}, fb [5..273], btMode ∈ {0,1}, numHashBytes ∈ {2,3,4}, mc [1..(1<<30)], writeEndMark ∈ {0,1}, numThreads ∈ {1,2}.
Use after LzmaEncProps_Init or after manual edits before calling LzmaEnc_SetProps.

functions.name: LzmaEncProps_GetDictSize
functions.description: Returns the effective dictionary size that would be used for the given properties (possibly adjusted based on reduceSize/platform constraints). Useful for planning buffers or validating settings.
requirements: props2 must be a non-null pointer to a valid CLzmaEncProps (initialized/normalized recommended).

functions.name: LzmaEnc_Create
functions.description: Creates an LZMA encoder instance using the provided allocator and returns an opaque handle for subsequent operations.
requirements: alloc must be a valid ISzAllocPtr providing allocation callbacks compatible with the encoder.
The returned handle must be destroyed with LzmaEnc_Destroy using the same allocator set(s).
On allocation failure the function may return NULL (not explicitly documented; typical behavior in this library).

functions.name: LzmaEnc_Destroy
functions.signature: void LzmaEnc_Destroy(CLzmaEncHandle p, ISzAllocPtr alloc, ISzAllocPtr allocBig);
functions.description: Destroys an LZMA encoder instance and frees resources using the provided allocators.
requirements: p must be a handle previously returned by LzmaEnc_Create and not already destroyed.
alloc and allocBig must be valid and must match the allocators used with this encoder (per library conventions).
Must be called exactly once for each successful LzmaEnc_Create to avoid leaks.

functions.name: LzmaEnc_SetProps
functions.description: Applies encoder properties to an LZMA encoder handle. Returns SZ_OK on success or an error code (e.g., SZ_ERROR_PARAM if a property is invalid). Call before encoding.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle created by LzmaEnc_Create.

props must be non-null and its fields should satisfy documented ranges: level [0..9]; dictSize: (1<<12)..(1<<27) on 32-bit, (1<<12)..(3<<29) on 64-bit; lc [0..8]; lp [0..4]; pb [0..4]; algo ∈ {0,1}; fb [5..273]; btMode ∈ {0,1}; numHashBytes ∈ {2,3,4}; mc [1..(1<<30)]; writeEndMark ∈ {0,1}; numThreads ∈ {1,2}.
Call before LzmaEnc_WriteProperties or encoding functions to ensure settings are in effect.
Check the returned SRes and handle non-SZ_OK values (e.g., SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_MEM).

functions.name: LzmaEnc_SetDataSize
functions.description: Hints the encoder about the expected uncompressed input size to optimize compression parameters (e.g., dictionary reduction when reduceSize is set). Use before encoding if the data size is known; use (UInt64)(Int64)-1 to indicate unknown size (per property default).
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle.
expectedDataSiize may be any 64-bit value; using (UInt64)(Int64)-1 indicates unknown (inferred from reduceSize documentation).
Call before LzmaEnc_Encode or LzmaEnc_MemEncode for best effect.

functions.name: LzmaEnc_WriteProperties
functions.description: Writes the encoder properties bytes for this handle into the provided buffer. The LZMA properties blob is LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5) bytes. On success, properties[0..*size-1] is filled and *size is set to the number of bytes written.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle with properties set (typically via LzmaEnc_SetProps or defaults).
properties must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
size must be non-null and on input must indicate the available buffer capacity; it must be at least LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5).
On success returns SZ_OK; on failure returns an SRes error (e.g., SZ_ERROR_PARAM if size too small, per common pattern; exact codes not fully specified).
Caller must check the returned SRes; do not use the output if non-SZ_OK.

functions.name: LzmaEnc_IsWriteEndMark
functions.description: Returns whether the encoder is configured to write an end-of-payload marker (end mark). Typically reflects props->writeEndMark (0 or 1).
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle.
Interpret the return as a boolean flag (0 = no end mark, non-zero = write end mark).

functions.name: LzmaEnc_Encode
functions.signature: SRes LzmaEnc_Encode(CLzmaEncHandle p, ISeqOutStream *outStream, ISeqInStream *inStream, ICompressProgress *progress, ISzAllocPtr alloc, ISzAllocPtr allocBig);
functions.description: Compresses data from an input stream to an output stream using the configured encoder handle. Reports progress via the optional progress callback. Returns SZ_OK on success or an SRes error (e.g., SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_WRITE, SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS, SZ_ERROR_THREAD).
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle with desired properties set.
outStream must be a non-null pointer to a valid ISeqOutStream implementation; its write callback must tolerate the encoder's calling pattern.
inStream must be a non-null pointer to a valid ISeqInStream implementation; its read callback must provide the requested data until EOF.
progress may be provided to receive progress notifications; behavior if NULL is not stated (unknown).
alloc and allocBig must be valid allocators consistent with the encoder.
Caller must check the returned SRes and handle non-SZ_OK codes including: SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_WRITE, SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS, SZ_ERROR_THREAD (as documented).

functions.name: LzmaEnc_MemEncode
functions.signature: SRes LzmaEnc_MemEncode(CLzmaEncHandle p, Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT srcLen, int writeEndMark, ICompressProgress *progress, ISzAllocPtr alloc, ISzAllocPtr allocBig);
functions.description: Compresses a memory buffer src/srcLen into dest with size destLen. Optionally writes an end marker depending on writeEndMark. Updates *destLen with the number of bytes written. Returns SZ_OK on success or an error (including SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF if dest is too small).
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle with properties set.
dest must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
destLen must be non-null; on input it must contain the capacity of dest in bytes; on output it is set to the number of bytes actually written.
src must be a non-null pointer to the input buffer of length srcLen.
srcLen can be zero or more; exact constraints not specified.
writeEndMark must be 0 or 1.
progress may be provided; behavior if NULL is not stated (unknown).
alloc and allocBig must be valid allocators.
Caller must check SRes and specifically handle SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF, which indicates output buffer overflow.

functions.name: LzmaEncode
functions.signature: SRes LzmaEncode(Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT srcLen, const CLzmaEncProps *props, Byte *propsEncoded, SizeT *propsSize, int writeEndMark, ICompressProgress *progress, ISzAllocPtr alloc, ISzAllocPtr allocBig);
functions.description: One-call convenience function to compress src/srcLen into dest, using props, and also produce the 5-byte LZMA properties in propsEncoded. Updates *destLen with output size and *propsSize with properties size. Returns SZ_OK on success or an error code as documented for encoder functions.
requirements: dest must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
destLen must be non-null; on input it must contain the capacity of dest; on output it is set to bytes written. If too small, expect SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF (per general API docs).
src must be a non-null pointer to the input buffer of length srcLen.
props should point to a CLzmaEncProps with fields in documented ranges; whether NULL is allowed to imply defaults is not stated (unknown).
propsEncoded must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least LZMA_PROPS_SIZE (5) bytes to receive encoder properties.
propsSize must be non-null; on input it should indicate propsEncoded capacity (must be >= 5); on output it is set to bytes written (typically 5).
writeEndMark must be 0 or 1.
progress may be provided; behavior if NULL is not stated (unknown).
alloc and allocBig must be valid allocators.
Caller must check SRes and handle errors such as SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_WRITE (not applicable for memory output), SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF, SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS, SZ_ERROR_THREAD.

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_AllocateProbs
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Dec_AllocateProbs(CLzma2Dec *p, Byte prop, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: Allocate (or reallocate) probability/model structures for an LZMA2 decoder using the supplied property byte. Intended for cases where you want to allocate only the probability models (not the full dictionary) before decoding. Typical usage: construct CLzma2Dec, call Lzma2Dec_AllocateProbs with the LZMA2 properties byte, then later call Lzma2Dec_Allocate (or equivalent) and Lzma2Dec_Init before decoding. Returns SZ_OK on success; error codes follow LZMA SDK conventions.
requirements: p must point to a valid CLzma2Dec instance (usually zero-initialized via Lzma2Dec_Construct).
prop must be the 1-byte LZMA2 properties value for the stream being decoded.
alloc must be a valid allocator compatible with the LZMA SDK (ISzAllocPtr).
Must be called before decoding and typically before Lzma2Dec_Init.
On failure (SRes != SZ_OK), the caller must not attempt to decode until allocation succeeds.

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_Allocate
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Dec_Allocate(CLzma2Dec *p, Byte prop, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: Allocate all required internal structures for an LZMA2 decoder (including probability models and dictionary as needed) using the provided LZMA2 properties byte. Use this for standard setup prior to decoding. Returns SZ_OK on success; otherwise an error code (e.g., memory or property issues).
requirements: p must point to a valid CLzma2Dec instance (usually constructed with Lzma2Dec_Construct).
prop must be the LZMA2 1-byte property value from the compressed stream header.
alloc must be a valid ISzAllocPtr allocator.
Call this before Lzma2Dec_Init and any decode functions.
If this call fails, do not call decode functions until a successful allocate has been performed.

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_Init
functions.description: Initialize or reinitialize an LZMA2 decoder state for decoding a (new) LZMA2 stream with previously allocated resources. Call after Allocate/AllocateProbs and before the first decode call, and when starting a new stream with the same decoder instance.
requirements: p must point to a CLzma2Dec whose internal resources have been allocated via Lzma2Dec_Allocate (or at least probabilities via Lzma2Dec_AllocateProbs combined with additional allocations as required by your workflow).
Must be called before the first decoding call for a stream, and when starting decoding of a new stream with the same state object.

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_DecodeToDic
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Dec_DecodeToDic(CLzma2Dec *p, SizeT dicLimit, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status);
functions.description: Decode LZMA2-compressed data from src into the decoder's internal dictionary until dicLimit (dictionary write limit) is reached, input is exhausted, or finish conditions are met. Use for streaming to a caller-managed dictionary buffer. The finishMode controls behavior only when the output limit is reached: LZMA_FINISH_ANY uses the minimal input; LZMA_FINISH_END requires an end marker. On SZ_OK, status indicates whether the stream finished with a marker, is not finished, or needs more input; returns SZ_ERROR_DATA on data errors.
requirements: p must be allocated via Lzma2Dec_Allocate (and initialized via Lzma2Dec_Init) before calling.
dicLimit must be within the bounds of the decoder's dictionary capacity; it is the limit up to which data may be written.
src must point to the input buffer; srcLen must be non-null and on input contain the available source size; on return it is updated to the number of bytes consumed.
status must be a valid pointer to receive an ELzmaStatus code.
finishMode must be a valid ELzmaFinishMode value; it only affects behavior if the output limit is reached.
Caller must check the returned SRes and the out-status to decide whether more input/output processing is needed or if decoding has finished.
Do not pass overlapping memory between src and the internal dictionary (standard non-overlap requirement).

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_DecodeToBuf
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Dec_DecodeToBuf(CLzma2Dec *p, Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status);
functions.description: Decode LZMA2-compressed data from src into the caller-provided output buffer dest, writing up to *destLen bytes. The function stops when the output limit is reached, input is exhausted, or finish conditions are met. The finishMode controls behavior only when the output limit is reached. On SZ_OK, status reports whether the stream finished with an end marker or is not finished; SZ_ERROR_DATA indicates a data error.
requirements: p must be allocated via Lzma2Dec_Allocate and initialized via Lzma2Dec_Init before calling.
dest must point to a writable buffer; destLen must be non-null and on input contain the buffer capacity; on return it is updated to the number of bytes written.
src must point to the input buffer; srcLen must be non-null and on input contain the available source size; on return it is updated to the number of bytes consumed.
status must be a valid pointer to receive an ELzmaStatus code.
finishMode must be a valid ELzmaFinishMode; it only matters when the output limit is reached.
Caller must examine both SRes and status to determine completion and whether more input/output is required.
Input and output buffers must not overlap.

functions.name: Lzma2Dec_Parse
functions.signature: ELzma2ParseStatus Lzma2Dec_Parse(CLzma2Dec *p, SizeT outSize, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, int checkFinishBlock);
functions.description: Parse the LZMA2 stream structure without decoding LZMA chunk payloads, advancing input up to the next independent block or the next chunk header. Returns either an ELzmaStatus value or one of the LZMA2_PARSE_STATUS_* codes indicating discovery of a new block or a new chunk (with CLzma2Dec::unpackSize set for that chunk). If checkFinishBlock is set, parsing will ensure the full input is read when the internal decoder.dicPos reaches the block maximum.
requirements: p must point to a valid and initialized CLzma2Dec (state should correspond to the stream being parsed).
outSize specifies the current output limit context for parsing; must be non-negative and within the decoder's expected range (exact bounds unknown from header).
src must point to the input buffer to parse; srcLen must be non-null and provide available input size on entry; it is updated with the number of bytes consumed.
checkFinishBlock must be 0 or 1; when 1, the parser must read full input data if decoder.dicPos reaches blockMax (per comment).
Caller must handle that the function may return standard LZMA_STATUS_* codes or the LZMA2_PARSE_STATUS_* codes and act accordingly.
Since the parser does not decode LZMA chunks, the caller must be prepared to provide full LZMA chunk data if subsequent decoding is intended.

functions.name: Lzma2Decode
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Decode(Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, Byte prop, ELzmaFinishMode finishMode, ELzmaStatus *status, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: One-call LZMA2 decode convenience API. Decompresses from src to dest using the provided LZMA2 property byte. destLen and srcLen are in/out: on input they specify available sizes; on return they are updated to the actual bytes written/consumed. finishMode controls behavior only when the output limit (*destLen) is reached. Returns SZ_OK on success (status indicates FINISHED_WITH_MARK or NOT_FINISHED), SZ_ERROR_DATA on data errors, SZ_ERROR_MEM on memory allocation errors, SZ_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for unsupported properties, and SZ_ERROR_INPUT_EOF if more input is required.
requirements: dest must point to a writable buffer; destLen must be non-null and contain the available output capacity on input; on return it contains the number of bytes written.
src must point to the compressed data; srcLen must be non-null and contain the available input size on input; on return it contains the number of bytes consumed.
prop must be the LZMA2 property byte corresponding to the compressed stream.
finishMode must be a valid ELzmaFinishMode; it is only meaningful when the decoder reaches the output limit.
status must be a valid pointer to receive an ELzmaStatus result.
alloc must be a valid allocator (ISzAllocPtr) to allow the function to allocate internal structures.
Caller must check both the SRes return code and the status output to determine completion and whether additional input/output is required.

functions.name: Lzma2EncProps_Init
functions.description: Initializes a CLzma2EncProps structure to default encoder properties for LZMA2. Typical usage is to zero/initialize a props object before optionally adjusting fields and passing it to Lzma2Enc_SetProps.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable CLzma2EncProps instance.
Call before using the props with Lzma2Enc_SetProps.
Any fields not explicitly set by the caller after initialization will retain the defaults set by this function (exact defaults are not described in this header).

functions.name: Lzma2EncProps_Normalize
functions.description: Normalizes a CLzma2EncProps structure, fixing or constraining fields to acceptable ranges for the encoder. Use after customizing CLzma2EncProps to ensure it meets encoder requirements.
requirements: p must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable CLzma2EncProps instance.
Should be called after the caller modifies props fields and before Lzma2Enc_SetProps (inferred from name and standard 7-Zip patterns; exact normalization rules are not specified in this header).

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_Create
functions.description: Creates and returns an LZMA2 encoder handle using the provided allocators. Use this handle with subsequent Lzma2Enc_* functions and destroy it with Lzma2Enc_Destroy.
requirements: alloc must be a valid allocator pointer (ISzAllocPtr) suitable for standard allocations required by the encoder.
allocBig should be a valid allocator pointer for large allocations; if NULL usage is supported or not is unknown (not specified).
Must be successfully called before any other functions that take CLzma2EncHandle.

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_Destroy
functions.description: Destroys an encoder handle created by Lzma2Enc_Create and frees associated resources.
requirements: p must be a handle previously returned by Lzma2Enc_Create or NULL.
After this call, p must not be used again.
Should be called exactly once for each successful Lzma2Enc_Create to avoid leaks.

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_SetProps
functions.description: Applies the specified LZMA2 encoder properties to an existing encoder handle. Returns an SRes status (e.g., SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_THREAD).
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle created by Lzma2Enc_Create.
props must be a valid, non-null pointer to a properly initialized CLzma2EncProps (typically initialized via Lzma2EncProps_Init and optionally normalized via Lzma2EncProps_Normalize).
Caller must check the returned SRes and handle errors such as SZ_ERROR_PARAM (incorrect parameter in props) and other codes listed in the header comment.

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_SetDataSize
functions.description: Hints or sets the expected input data size for the encoder. This may influence block sizing or stream headers. Exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle created by Lzma2Enc_Create.
expectedDataSiize is a UInt64 size hint; accepted special values or effects are not specified in this header.
Should be called before encoding to ensure the encoder can use the hint (inferred from name; exact timing not specified).

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_WriteProperties
functions.description: Returns the single-byte LZMA2 properties value describing the encoder settings, suitable for writing to a container/header that stores LZMA2 properties. Exact mapping of bits is not documented here.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle created by Lzma2Enc_Create.
Properties typically depend on the encoder’s configured props; calling after Lzma2Enc_SetProps is recommended (inferred; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: Lzma2Enc_Encode2
functions.signature: SRes Lzma2Enc_Encode2(CLzma2EncHandle p, ISeqOutStream *outStream, Byte *outBuf, size_t *outBufSize, ISeqInStream *inStream, const Byte *inData, size_t inDataSize, ICompressProgress *progress);
functions.description: Encodes data using LZMA2. Supports stream-to-stream and buffer-based I/O: you can provide output via outStream or via an output buffer pair (outBuf/outBufSize), and input via inStream or via an input buffer (inData/inDataSize). Returns SRes status codes including SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_MEM, SZ_ERROR_PARAM, SZ_ERROR_WRITE, SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF (output buffer overflow for the buffer variant), SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS, SZ_ERROR_THREAD.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle created by Lzma2Enc_Create and configured as needed (e.g., via Lzma2Enc_SetProps).

Exactly one output mechanism should be provided: either outStream is non-null, or outBuf and outBufSize are both non-null (inference from signature and documented SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF for the buffer variant; not explicitly stated).

If using the buffer output mode: outBuf and outBufSize must be valid pointers; *outBufSize must specify the size of outBuf on input, and will be updated with the number of bytes written (typical 7-Zip convention; exact in/out convention is not explicitly described here).
Exactly one input mechanism should be provided: either inStream is non-null, or inData with inDataSize specifies the input buffer (inference from signature).
inDataSize must match the size of the inData buffer when using buffer input.
progress may be NULL; if provided, progress callbacks may be invoked and SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS can be returned if the operation is interrupted (per header comment).
Caller must check and handle the returned SRes code, including SZ_ERROR_WRITE from outStream callbacks and SZ_ERROR_OUTPUT_EOF when the provided outBuf is too small.

functions.name: Xz_ReadVarInt
functions.signature: unsigned Xz_ReadVarInt(const Byte *p, size_t maxSize, UInt64 *value);
functions.description: Parses an XZ-format variable-length integer from the buffer p, reading at most maxSize bytes, and writes the decoded value to *value. Returns the number of bytes consumed (0 typically indicates an error or incomplete varint). Intended for reading sizes/ids from XZ headers and indexes.
requirements: p must point to a readable buffer of at least maxSize bytes.
value must be a valid, writable pointer.
maxSize must be > 0.
The buffer must contain a complete, well-formed XZ variable-length integer within maxSize bytes.
Caller should treat a return of 0 as failure to parse (e.g., malformed or incomplete value).

functions.name: Xz_WriteVarInt
functions.description: Encodes the 64-bit integer v into XZ variable-length integer format and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written. Used for producing XZ headers/indices.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the encoded value. The worst-case size for XZ varints is up to 9 bytes (inferred from common varint encodings).
No additional alignment requirements are specified.
Caller is responsible for using the returned size to advance the output pointer.

functions.name: XzBlock_Parse
functions.description: Parses an XZ Block Header from the supplied header buffer and fills the CXzBlock structure p (filters, flags, optional pack/unpack sizes). Returns an SRes status code (SZ_OK on success).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzBlock pointer; its fields will be overwritten.
header must point to a complete XZ Block Header buffer as obtained from XzBlock_ReadHeader.
The header must describe at most XZ_NUM_FILTERS_MAX (4) filters and comply with flags; unsupported flags cause an error (see XzBlock_HasUnsupportedFlags).

functions.name: XzBlock_ReadHeader
functions.description: Reads and parses the next XZ Block Header (or detects an Index instead) from inStream, fills p, and reports whether an Index was encountered via *isIndex and the header size via *headerSizeRes. Returns SRes (SZ_OK on success).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzBlock pointer.
inStream must be a valid input stream positioned at the start of an XZ Block Header or Index.
isIndex must be a valid, writable pointer; on return non-zero indicates Index instead of a Block.
headerSizeRes must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the Block Header size.
Caller must handle SRes error codes: SZ_ERROR_DATA/UNSUPPORTED/CRC/etc. as appropriate (inferred from library patterns).

functions.name: XzCheck_Init
functions.description: Initializes the incremental XZ integrity check state p for the specified check mode (e.g., CRC32, CRC64, SHA256). Must be called before Update/Final.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzCheck pointer.
mode must be one of XZ_CHECK_* values supported by the build (e.g., XZ_CHECK_NO, XZ_CHECK_CRC32, XZ_CHECK_CRC64, XZ_CHECK_SHA256).
Caller must re-initialize before reusing the object for a new stream.

functions.name: XzCheck_Update
functions.signature: void XzCheck_Update(CXzCheck *p, const void *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Feeds data into the initialized XZ integrity check state p. Accumulates the checksum over successive calls.
requirements: p must have been initialized with XzCheck_Init.
data must point to at least size bytes when size > 0; data may be NULL only if size == 0.
May be called multiple times before XzCheck_Final.

functions.name: XzCheck_Final
functions.description: Finalizes the XZ integrity check computation and writes the resulting digest to digest. Returns the digest size in bytes or 0 on error/unsupported mode. After finalization, p may need to be reinitialized before reuse.
requirements: p must have been initialized and updated as needed.
digest must point to a buffer large enough for the selected check type: use XzFlags_GetCheckSize/XzFlags_GetCheckType to size appropriately (e.g., 0, 4, 8, 32 bytes for NO/CRC32/CRC64/SHA256).

functions.name: XzFlags_GetCheckSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the integrity check field for the stream flags f (derived from the check type in f).
requirements: f should be supported (XzFlags_IsSupported(f) should be true).
Caller should not assume non-zero result when check type is XZ_CHECK_NO (size may be 0).

functions.name: Xz_ParseHeader
functions.description: Parses an XZ Stream Header from the buffer buf, validates its CRC, and outputs the stream flags into *p. Returns SRes (SZ_OK on success; SZ_ERROR_NO_ARCHIVE on signature/CRC/padding errors per comments).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to receive stream flags.
buf must point to a buffer containing a complete XZ Stream Header of size XZ_STREAM_HEADER_SIZE bytes.
The header must start with XZ signature XZ_SIG and have a valid CRC.

functions.name: Xz_ReadHeader
functions.description: Reads and parses an XZ Stream Header from inStream and outputs the stream flags into *p. Returns SRes (SZ_OK on success; SZ_ERROR_NO_ARCHIVE on invalid signature/CRC/padding per comments).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to receive stream flags.
inStream must be a valid input stream positioned at the start of an XZ stream header.
Caller must handle SRes return codes and stop/continue accordingly.

functions.name: Xz_Construct
functions.description: Initializes an empty CXzStream structure p to a safe default state (no blocks, zero sizes). Call before filling the stream or reading indexes.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer.
Must be called before Xz_Free on the same object.
No allocator is needed at construct time.

functions.name: Xz_Free
functions.description: Releases resources owned by CXzStream p using the provided allocator alloc and resets it to an empty state.
requirements: p must have been initialized (e.g., via Xz_Construct or filled by reader).
alloc must be the same allocator used for any dynamic allocations inside p.
It is safe to call with an already-empty stream.

functions.name: Xz_GetUnpackSize
functions.description: Returns the total uncompressed size across all blocks in the XZ stream p, or XZ_SIZE_OVERFLOW if the sum overflows 64-bit signed range.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a properly constructed/filled CXzStream.
Caller must check for XZ_SIZE_OVERFLOW ((UInt64)(Int64)-1) as an overflow indicator.

functions.name: Xz_GetPackSize
functions.description: Returns the total compressed size (including headers/footers as accounted by the implementation) of the XZ stream p, or XZ_SIZE_OVERFLOW on overflow.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a properly constructed/filled CXzStream.
Caller must handle XZ_SIZE_OVERFLOW ((UInt64)(Int64)-1).

functions.name: Xzs_Construct
functions.description: Initializes a CXzs structure (a collection of CXzStream entries) to an empty, safe state.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzs pointer.
Must be called before Xzs_Free on the same object.

functions.name: Xzs_Free
functions.description: Frees resources for the CXzs collection p using allocator alloc and resets it to empty.
requirements: p must have been initialized (e.g., via Xzs_Construct or filled by reader).
alloc must be the allocator used for allocations inside p.

functions.name: Xzs_ReadBackward
functions.signature: SRes Xzs_ReadBackward(CXzs *p, ILookInStream *inStream, Int64 *startOffset, ICompressProgress *progress, ISzAllocPtr alloc);
functions.description: Scans the input stream inStream backwards from the end to locate and parse XZ stream(s) Index and Headers, filling p with stream descriptors. Reports the start offset of the earliest stream in *startOffset. Returns SRes.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzs pointer; it will be filled with stream metadata and must be freed via Xzs_Free.
inStream must be a valid random-access look-ahead input stream positioned appropriately (typically at or before the end).
startOffset must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the first stream start offset.
progress may be NULL or a valid progress callback depending on implementation; handle errors SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS accordingly (inferred from common patterns).
alloc must be a valid allocator for internal allocations.
Caller must handle SRes codes including SZ_ERROR_NO_ARCHIVE/ARCHIVE/DATA/CRC/etc.

functions.name: Xzs_GetNumBlocks
functions.description: Returns the total number of blocks across all streams in the CXzs collection p.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a constructed/filled CXzs.

functions.name: Xzs_GetUnpackSize
functions.description: Returns the total uncompressed size across all streams in the CXzs collection p.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a constructed/filled CXzs.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_Construct
functions.description: Constructs and initializes the XZ unpacker state p with the provided allocator alloc. Must be called before decoding and paired with XzUnpacker_Free.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable CXzUnpacker pointer.
alloc must be a valid allocator; aligned allocation is preferred for performance (comment).
Call XzUnpacker_Free to release resources.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_Init
functions.description: Resets the unpacker state p for a new decoding session. Use before the decoding loop for partial-buffer or direct-buffer modes.
requirements: p must have been constructed via XzUnpacker_Construct.
Must be called before the first XzUnpacker_Code of a session, and again before reusing the unpacker for a new input.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_SetOutBuf
functions.description: Sets the direct output buffer and its size for direct-output mode (Interface-2/3). When used, pass dest == NULL to XzUnpacker_Code.
requirements: p must have been constructed (and typically initialized via XzUnpacker_Init).
outBuf must point to a writable buffer of size outBufSize when outBufSize > 0; may be NULL only if outBufSize == 0 (no output).
Must be called before using XzUnpacker_Code with dest == NULL (direct-output mode).

functions.name: XzUnpacker_Free
functions.description: Frees resources associated with the unpacker p. After this call, p must be reconstructed before reuse.
requirements: p must have been constructed via XzUnpacker_Construct.
Safe to call when partially initialized; it will clean internal resources.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_Code
functions.signature: SRes XzUnpacker_Code(CXzUnpacker *p, Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, int srcFinished, ECoderFinishMode finishMode, ECoderStatus *status);
functions.description: Incrementally decodes XZ data from src into dest. Supports two modes: partial-output buffers (dest != NULL) and direct-output buffer mode (dest == NULL after XzUnpacker_SetOutBuf). Updates *destLen with bytes produced and *srcLen with bytes consumed. The finishMode controls behavior when output limit is reached. Returns SRes and sets *status to indicate progress (e.g., CODER_STATUS_NOT_FINISHED, CODER_STATUS_NEEDS_MORE_INPUT).
requirements: p must have been constructed and initialized via XzUnpacker_Init for the current session.
If using partial-output mode, dest must point to a writable buffer of at least *destLen bytes on input; on return, *destLen is updated to bytes written.

If using direct-output mode, dest must be NULL and a buffer must have been set via XzUnpacker_SetOutBuf; in that case, *destLen is still updated to the number of bytes fully unpacked into the internal out buffer within this call.
src must point to readable data; *srcLen on input supplies available bytes and is updated to consumed bytes on return.
srcFinished is non-zero if no more input will be provided (end-of-input hint).
finishMode must be CODER_FINISH_ANY or CODER_FINISH_END as defined.
status must be a valid, writable pointer; it receives the coder status.

Caller must handle SRes results described in the header comments (SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_MEM/DATA/UNSUPPORTED/CRC/NO_ARCHIVE, etc.) and check CODER_STATUS to decide whether to continue, supply more input, or stop.
When SZ_OK with CODER_STATUS_NEEDS_MORE_INPUT, the caller may need to check XzUnpacker_IsStreamWasFinished to determine if current stream finished.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_CodeFull
functions.signature: SRes XzUnpacker_CodeFull(CXzUnpacker *p, Byte *dest, SizeT *destLen, const Byte *src, SizeT *srcLen, ECoderFinishMode finishMode, ECoderStatus *status);
functions.description: Convenience helper that decodes the entire input buffer src to the output buffer dest in one call (Interface-3), internally using direct-output mode. Updates *destLen and *srcLen. Returns SRes and sets *status.
requirements: p must have been constructed; this function internally sets up direct-output mode.
dest must point to a writable buffer with capacity specified via *destLen on input; on return, *destLen is updated to bytes written.
src must point to readable data; *srcLen on input supplies available bytes and is updated to consumed bytes on return.
finishMode and status have the same semantics as in XzUnpacker_Code.
Caller must handle SRes and status results as documented.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_IsStreamWasFinished
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current XZ stream was fully finished (end marker reached) during decoding; zero otherwise. Useful when XzUnpacker_Code returns CODER_STATUS_NEEDS_MORE_INPUT to distinguish end-of-stream from more-streams cases.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to an initialized/used CXzUnpacker.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_GetExtraSize
functions.description: Reports the number of unconfirmed bytes when the unpacker is in STREAM_HEADER or STREAM_PADDING states. These bytes may be trailing data after the xz archive or the start of a next xz stream. Useful to determine the exact archive size after decoding attempts that ended with NEEDS_MORE_INPUT or SZ_ERROR_NO_ARCHIVE.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to an initialized/used CXzUnpacker.
Call after XzUnpacker_Code in scenarios described to query trailing/extra data size.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_PrepareToRandomBlockDecoding
functions.description: Prepares the unpacker state p for random block decoding when stream flags are already known and blocks will be decoded individually.
requirements: p must have been constructed and initialized (XzUnpacker_Init) for the new session.
Caller must set p->streamFlags before calling, per comment.
Follow the documented loop: XzUnpacker_Code then XzUnpacker_IsBlockFinished to detect block completion.

functions.name: XzUnpacker_IsBlockFinished
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the current block being decoded is finished, zero otherwise. Intended for random block decoding workflows.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to an unpacker engaged in block decoding.

functions.name: XzDecMtProps_Init
functions.description: Initializes the multi-threaded decoder properties structure p with defaults (buffer sizes, thread count, memory limits, and flags).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer.
Must be called before using the properties in XzDecMt_Decode.

functions.name: XzDecMt_Create
functions.description: Creates and returns a multi-threaded XZ decoder handle using the provided allocators (aligned allocation is used by the implementation). Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: alloc must be a valid allocator for general allocations.
allocMid should be provided for large/aligned allocations (as per comment).
Caller must destroy the handle with XzDecMt_Destroy.

functions.name: XzDecMt_Destroy
functions.description: Destroys the multi-threaded XZ decoder handle p and frees associated resources.
requirements: p must be a handle previously returned by XzDecMt_Create; passing NULL is allowed by common patterns but not explicitly documented.
After destruction, the handle is invalid.

functions.name: XzStatInfo_Clear
functions.description: Resets/clears the CXzStatInfo structure p (sizes, counts, flags, and result codes) to defaults before/after a decode.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer.
Call before reusing the stat structure for a new decode session.

functions.name: XzDecMt_Decode
functions.signature: SRes XzDecMt_Decode(CXzDecMtHandle p, const CXzDecMtProps *props, const UInt64 *outDataSize, int finishMode, ISeqOutStream *outStream, ISeqInStream *inStream, CXzStatInfo *stat, int *isMT, ICompressProgress *progress);
functions.description: Decodes XZ stream(s) from inStream to outStream using the multi-threaded decoder handle p and properties props. Optionally limits decoding to outDataSize bytes. finishMode controls whether partial unpacking is allowed (0) or streams must be finished (1). Fills stat with progress and result information and sets *isMT to 0 if the single-threaded path was used. Returns SRes (see exhaustive list of possible errors in the header comment).
requirements: p must be a valid handle created by XzDecMt_Create.
props should be initialized via XzDecMtProps_Init.
outDataSize may be NULL (undefined total) or point to a limit value.
finishMode must be 0 (partial allowed) or 1 (must finish).
outStream must be a valid output stream; the decoder writes decoded bytes to it and may return SZ_ERROR_WRITE on failures.
inStream must be a valid input stream; read failures are reported as SZ_ERROR_READ or MY_SRes_HRESULT_FROM_WRes.
stat must be a valid, writable pointer; it is filled with sizes, counts, and result codes.
isMT must be a valid, writable pointer; it will be set to 0 if the ST path is used, non-zero otherwise.
progress may be a valid progress callback; errors are reported as SZ_ERROR_PROGRESS.
Caller must handle all SRes outcomes listed in the comment (SZ_OK, SZ_ERROR_MEM/NO_ARCHIVE/ARCHIVE/DATA/CRC/INPUT_EOF/WRITE/READ/PROGRESS/threading errors).

functions.name: XzFilterProps_Init
functions.description: Initialize a CXzFilterProps structure to default values suitable for use with the XZ encoder (e.g., filter id, delta, ip fields). Call this before setting custom filter properties or embedding CXzFilterProps in CXzProps.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a CXzFilterProps instance.
Call before passing CXzFilterProps to other XZ encoding APIs.
The structure should not be assumed initialized prior to this call; contents are unspecified until initialized.

functions.name: XzProps_Init
functions.description: Initialize an XZ encoder properties structure (CXzProps) to defaults, including nested LZMA2 and filter properties and container-level options (checkId, blockSize, threading, etc.). Use this before modifying fields or passing properties to the encoder.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to a CXzProps instance.
Call before using CXzProps with XzEnc_SetProps or Xz_Encode.
Fields not explicitly set by the caller after initialization will remain at their library-defined defaults.

functions.name: XzEnc_Create
functions.description: Create and return an XZ encoder handle using the provided allocators. The handle is used with subsequent XzEnc_* calls to configure and run streaming XZ compression.
requirements: alloc must be a valid allocator compatible with the library’s ISzAlloc interface.
allocBig must be a valid allocator for large allocations (may be the same as alloc depending on the environment).
Returns NULL on allocation/initialization failure (caller must check).
The returned handle must be destroyed with XzEnc_Destroy to avoid leaks.

functions.name: XzEnc_Destroy
functions.description: Destroy an XZ encoder handle created by XzEnc_Create and release all associated resources.
requirements: p must be a handle previously returned by XzEnc_Create, or NULL.
After this call, p becomes invalid and must not be reused.
Safe to call with NULL (based on common library patterns), but exact behavior is not explicitly documented; callers should avoid double-destroying the same handle.

functions.name: XzEnc_SetProps
functions.description: Apply encoder properties to an existing XZ encoder handle. Typically called after XzProps_Init and any property customization and before encoding.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle returned by XzEnc_Create.
props must point to an initialized CXzProps (initialize with XzProps_Init before modifying/using).
Must be called before XzEnc_Encode to take effect.
Returns an SRes status code; caller must check for success and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: XzEnc_SetDataSize
functions.description: Optionally inform the encoder of the expected input size to improve header/size writing or compression decisions. Note: the parameter name in the header is spelled expectedDataSiize (double 'i').
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle returned by XzEnc_Create.
May be called before XzEnc_Encode; effect after encoding begins is unspecified.
expectedDataSiize can be any 64-bit size; special values (e.g., unknown) are not specified here.
This function does not report errors; callers cannot detect invalid size acceptance through the return value.

functions.name: XzEnc_Encode
functions.signature: SRes XzEnc_Encode(CXzEncHandle p, ISeqOutStream *outStream, ISeqInStream *inStream, ICompressProgress *progress);
functions.description: Run streaming XZ encoding using the configured encoder handle, reading from inStream and writing the XZ container to outStream. Optionally reports progress via progress if provided.
requirements: p must be a valid encoder handle configured as needed (e.g., XzEnc_SetProps called if non-defaults are desired).
outStream must be a valid ISeqOutStream implementation and remain valid for the duration of the call.
inStream must be a valid ISeqInStream implementation and remain valid for the duration of the call.
progress may be NULL or a valid ICompressProgress implementation (NULL acceptability is inferred; exact requirement not explicitly stated).
Returns an SRes status code; caller must check and handle non-success values.
Should not be called concurrently on the same handle from multiple threads (thread-safety not documented; treat the handle as non-thread-safe).

functions.name: Xz_Encode
functions.signature: SRes Xz_Encode(ISeqOutStream *outStream, ISeqInStream *inStream, const CXzProps *props, ICompressProgress *progress);
functions.description: One-shot helper to encode an input stream to XZ format with the specified properties, writing to outStream. Internally creates and configures an encoder handle, runs encoding, then cleans up.
requirements: outStream must be a valid ISeqOutStream implementation.
inStream must be a valid ISeqInStream implementation.
props must point to an initialized CXzProps (initialize with XzProps_Init; may be modified as needed before the call).
progress may be NULL or a valid ICompressProgress implementation (NULL acceptability is inferred; exact requirement not explicitly stated).
Returns an SRes status code; caller must check and handle errors.

functions.name: Xz_EncodeEmpty
functions.description: Write an empty XZ stream (no data blocks) to outStream. Useful for representing empty payloads in XZ container form.
requirements: outStream must be a valid ISeqOutStream implementation and writable for the duration of the call.
Returns an SRes status code; caller must check and handle errors.

functions.name: SzGetNextFolderItem
functions.description: Parses the next folder (compression pipeline description) from the serialized 7z metadata buffer into f. Expected usage: iterate over CSzData while extracting folder definitions during archive parsing. Returns an SRes status code.
requirements: f must be a valid, writable pointer to CSzFolder.
sd must be a valid pointer to a CSzData structure with sd->Data pointing to readable memory of length sd->Size.
Only default methods (per comment in header) are supported by CSzCoderInfo/CSzFolder; non-default methods may not be handled.
Caller should ensure sd contains enough bytes for the next item; on insufficient data, an error SRes may be returned (exact codes unknown).

functions.name: SzAr_GetFolderUnpackSize
functions.description: Returns the total unpack (decompressed) size of the specified folder within the archive structure p. Useful to plan buffer sizes for decoding a folder.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a populated CSzAr.
folderIndex must refer to an existing folder (0 <= folderIndex < p->NumFolders).

functions.name: SzAr_DecodeFolder
functions.signature: SRes SzAr_DecodeFolder(const CSzAr *p, UInt32 folderIndex, ILookInStream *stream, UInt64 startPos, Byte *outBuffer, size_t outSize, ISzAllocPtr allocMain);
functions.description: Decodes (decompresses) the specified folder from the input stream into the caller-provided output buffer. Returns an SRes status code. Intended to extract the entire folder’s unpacked data in one call.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a populated CSzAr.
folderIndex must be within the range of folders defined by p.
stream must be a valid ILookInStream capable of providing the archive’s compressed data.
startPos is the start position in the stream for the folder’s packed data (caller must supply the correct position).
outBuffer must point to a writable buffer of size at least outSize bytes.
allocMain must be a valid allocator pointer (per 7zTypes.h).

functions.name: SzArEx_Init
functions.description: Initializes a CSzArEx structure to a clean state before use (e.g., before opening an archive).
requirements: p must be a valid, writable pointer to CSzArEx.

functions.name: SzArEx_Free
functions.description: Releases all resources owned by a CSzArEx that were allocated during open/extract operations, using the provided allocator.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to an initialized CSzArEx (initialized by SzArEx_Init and possibly populated by SzArEx_Open).
alloc must be the same allocator (or compatible) that was used for allocations associated with p.

functions.description: Returns the absolute stream position (offset) for a specific packed stream of a given folder in the archive represented by p.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a populated CSzArEx.
folderIndex must be a valid folder index within p->db.NumFolders.
indexInFolder must reference a valid pack stream within the specified folder.

functions.description: Computes the total packed size for a folder and stores it in resSize. Returns 0/non-zero status (exact convention not documented here).

folderIndex must be within range of folders.
resSize must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the size.

functions.name: SzArEx_GetFileNameUtf16
functions.signature: size_t SzArEx_GetFileNameUtf16(const CSzArEx *p, size_t fileIndex, UInt16 *dest);
functions.description: Retrieves a file’s name in UTF-16-LE. If dest is NULL, returns the required buffer length in 16-bit code units including the null terminator. If dest is non-NULL, writes the UTF-16-LE name (null-terminated) and returns the number of 16-bit code units written, including the terminator.
requirements: p must be a valid pointer to a populated CSzArEx.
fileIndex must be a valid file index (0 <= fileIndex < p->NumFiles).
If dest is non-NULL, the caller must provide a buffer of at least the size returned when calling with dest == NULL, measured in 16-bit characters.
dest receives UTF-16-LE code units and must be aligned for UInt16 where required by the platform.

functions.signature: SRes SzArEx_Extract(const CSzArEx *db, ILookInStream *inStream, UInt32 fileIndex, UInt32 *blockIndex, Byte **outBuffer, size_t *outBufferSize, size_t *offset, size_t *outSizeProcessed, ISzAllocPtr allocMain, ISzAllocPtr allocTemp);
functions.description: Extracts one file from the 7z archive. Supports solid-block caching: pass back blockIndex, outBuffer, and outBufferSize from a previous call to reuse a decompressed solid block for faster subsequent extracts. Returns an SRes status code.
requirements: db must be a valid pointer to an opened CSzArEx.
inStream must be a valid ILookInStream for the underlying archive data.
fileIndex must be a valid file index in the archive.
outBuffer must be a valid pointer to a Byte* variable; on first call for a given archive, *outBuffer must be 0 (per header comment).
outBufferSize must be a valid pointer to a size_t variable; it is used with outBuffer for caching a solid block.
